module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 250

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/250](https://www.erdosproblems.com/250)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos250

/--
Is
$$
  \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\sigma(n)}{2^n}
$$
irrational? Here $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of divisors function.

The answer is yes, as shown by Nesterenko [Ne96].

[Ne96] Nesterenko, Yu V., _Modular functions and transcendence questions_,
Mat. Sb. 187 *9* (1996), 1319--1348.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos250.lean#L97"]
theorem erdos_250  : (∀ x, HasSum (fun (n : ℕ) => σ 1 n / (2 : ℝ) ^ n) x → Irrational x) ↔
    answer(True):= by
  sorry

end Erdos250

reformulations.difference: The declaration uses a universal HasSum implication over all natural indices, rather than directly asserting irrationality of the sum indexed by positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib's σ 1 n is the sum of the positive divisors of n, with σ 1 0 = 0. Thus the additional zero-index term vanishes. The series is summable: its nonnegative terms are bounded by n²/2ⁿ, using sigma_le_pow_succ. Consequently the HasSum hypothesis is satisfiable, its real sum is unique, and '∀ x, HasSum f x → Irrational x' is equivalent to irrationality of the positive-index sum. The outer equivalence with answer(True) preserves this affirmative claim. Review250.source_equivalence proves the complete equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without invoking the problem theorem or sorry.
